assessment.nobel_worthiness: Changed how economists and policymakers understand technology, task content and import competition as drivers of labour demand, wages and local labour-market adjustment. The empirical designs are transparent and the findings have been widely replicated or re-examined, and they have shaped policy debate.
assessment.attribution: Autor and Hanson are the central figures: the task-based framework and the China-shock work with Dorn. Dorn is a close co-author and Katz is a major contributor to the skill-biased change literature. Limiting the award to two or three names requires a judgement about who is core.
assessment.maturity: The China-shock and task-polarization work is roughly 10 to 20 years old, with extensive follow-up, robustness checks and some contested interpretations. This is mature enough to rank first.
uncertainties: Debate over the magnitude and persistence of the China shock and over specification choices.
Whether the committee would favour Dorn or Katz over Hanson.
My knowledge of the latest re-examinations is incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities, together with the Taylor rule and the Calvo pricing device, underpins the modern theory and practice of monetary policy. Its influence on central banking is very large.
assessment.attribution: The credited list is large and the credit is diffuse: Calvo pricing, Taylor's rules and staggered contracts, Woodford's synthesis, Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Evans-style estimation, and Smets. A three-person award would leave out important contributors, and the choice is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of use in policy institutions. Its predictive performance was challenged after 2008 and again during the post-2021 inflation, which is the main substantive caveat.
uncertainties: Which three names best capture the core contribution.
Debate about the empirical performance of the framework in recent inflation episodes.
Some of the empirical foundations are model-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Systematically brought electoral rules, constitutions, state capacity and fiscal policy into formal and empirical economics, creating the modern field of political economics. The influence on later work in development, public and comparative political economy is substantial.
assessment.attribution: The Persson-Tabellini and Besley-Persson partnership structure makes a small group natural. The three named are the clearest core, though others, such as Acemoglu and Robinson, who have already been recognised, overlap with this area.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the main books and papers date from the 1990s and 2000s and have seen long empirical follow-up. Some cross-country empirical results rest on observational variation, so credibility varies across the programme.
uncertainties: Credibility of the cross-country identification in parts of the empirical work.
Overlap with already recognised work on institutions.
Possible perceived proximity of the Swedish-affiliated members, which is a disclosure rather than an adjudicated conflict.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki and Moore's credit-cycles model explains how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks, and it is a foundation of modern macro-finance and of how financial crises are analysed. It remains central to post-2008 macroeconomics.
assessment.attribution: The 1997 paper is the cleanly identified core contribution of Kiyotaki and Moore. Gertler and Gilchrist's financial accelerator work is related, and Bernanke and Gertler were recognised partly in the 2022 prize. Crediting only the first two is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of influence, extensive extensions and wide use in policy models.
uncertainties: Overlap with the financial-accelerator literature and the 2022 prize.
The theory is more influential than directly tested, and empirical identification of the collateral channel is mixed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The firm-heterogeneity trade model reoriented trade theory around exporters' selection and productivity, and it changed how the gains from trade are understood and measured. It also guided a large body of firm-level empirical work.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution, and Helpman's role runs through the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple paper and broader trade theory. Redding is a major contributor on quantitative spatial and trade models. Overlap with B003 and B041 raises attribution questions within trade.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of use, widely replicated in firm-level data across countries.
uncertainties: Choice of recipients within the trade field, given competing candidates.
Structural assumptions such as Pareto productivity distributions affect the quantitative conclusions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Connected optimal tax theory to estimable sufficient statistics and credible behavioural responses, so that taxation can be designed on empirical evidence. Policy influence is considerable.
assessment.attribution: Saez, Slemrod and Chetty each hold distinct pieces: Saez on optimal income taxation and top-income responses, Slemrod on tax-avoidance behaviour, Chetty on the sufficient-statistics approach and quasi-experimental evidence. Stantcheva is more junior. Credit is spread, and there is overlap with B013 and B021.
assessment.maturity: The elasticity of taxable income and sufficient-statistics work is now well established. Chetty's later work is newer and is partly credited elsewhere on the list.
uncertainties: Debate over the size and robustness of taxable-income elasticities.
Overlap with other Saez and Chetty candidacies.
Judgement about seniority and timing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification formalises how much can be learned under credible, weak assumptions rather than strong ones. This speaks directly to the credibility of empirical inference and has influenced applied work and the econometrics of incomplete models.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the founder of the approach. Tamer and Molinari did key work on inference and applications to incomplete models and moment inequalities.
assessment.maturity: Manski's contributions are decades old. Inference methods matured in the 2000s and 2010s. Applied uptake is still narrower than for point-identified methods.
uncertainties: Breadth of practical adoption relative to its conceptual influence.
Whether the committee prefers a pure econometric theory prize.
Dividing credit among Manski, Tamer and Molinari.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed that misallocation of inputs across firms can account for a large share of cross-country income differences, and gave a measurable framework for it. It reshaped the study of productivity and development.
assessment.attribution: The Hsieh-Klenow (2009) paper is the anchor, and Restuccia and Rogerson's related work on misallocation is closely tied. The Restuccia name is on the credited list but the contribution is split.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of influence. Measurement of misallocation has been debated, since measurement error, adjustment costs and markups can contaminate the estimates.
uncertainties: Robustness of the magnitude estimates to measurement error and model assumptions.
Credit split with Restuccia and Rogerson.
Possibly smaller scope than the higher-ranked candidates.
